rows.comment:
FAIL: Props placed on the table are unrealistic for real-life situations. 

The cork board with the color splotches on it adds no detail to the environment, making the overall shot look flat. We should potentially replace the cork board with some sort of artistic print or wall covering.

The lighting on the top lid of the laptop needs to be updated because the HP branding does not show through, and this is the primary focal point of the shot.

FAIL: There is no detail in the background of this, making the overall shot look incredibly flat and removing all depth to the shot. I'd also recommend that we choose a different prop for the situation to be placed on the table versus the glass, because this also contributes to the depth of the shot.
FAIL: The back bench of this shot actually has no seat or base to it, so the back cushions appear to be floating behind the table.
OK - would prefer an additional prop on the table just to give it a more "lived-in" situation.

FAIL: the back wall/partition and the glass partition do not align and create a false exit to the room that appears way too small.

In addition, the props used within the scene, specifically the clock, is a lot lower than it should be and are placed on a fabric partition. In addition, there are blank tiles sitting on the table as a prop, and these should be replaced with a more relevant prop for the scene.
OK - lighting can be improved on the overall product. In addition, given the shot framing, ideally there would be additional props on the table relevant to the scene.

FAIL - the prop selection on the table would likely not be a real life scenario.  One to two props should be included on the table that ensure that this is a "lived-in" environment (notebook, glasses, etc.).

FAIL - the water carafe is directly in front of the laptop, obstructing anybody's access to the prompt. 

In addition, the lighting on the top lid of the laptop is appears incorrect. The HP branding is not coming through.
FAIL - the chair on the right-hand side does not have a base or legs.
OK - recommendation to change the props to ensure that the environments look as if a person has been working at the table and to include a personal touch

OK - recommendation: to add additional detail to the background to populate the white space to ensure depth in the shot. Right now, the current wall covering tends to blend in with the table and product.
FAIL - laptop is not facing where an individual would sit. In addition, the table-to-bench alignment appears to be off, almost as if a person pushed the table out of the way so they could get up.

OK - recommend that we update the wall coverings to better populate the white space in the background and to add additional depth. This would include some form of wall art or other shelving to support the depth of this shot.

FAIL - the props look randomly placed and grouped together, as well as the furniture in the scene. Everything appears to be cluttered and does not appear as a real-life environment for a gaming environment.
OK
FAIL - printer crashes into the corkboard, and the corkboard is coming out of the wall.
OK - recommendation to swap out the light as a wall fixture and add some art to add additional detail to the scene and provide depth
OK - lacking detail in the background, making the overall environment appear flat
FAIL - prop placement of the clock would not be the correct placement in real life. Current placement appears to be at waist level.
FAIL - printer appears flush against the back wall, but the table is bending/warping in the environment.

FAIL - a lot of white space in the background, making the overall environment appear flat. In addition, there are no props (for example, a stack of paper, paper trays, etc.) that would contribute to the overall scene and environment.
OK - recommendation to update the wall coverings with some form of picture, abstract art, etc.

FAIL - placement of props within the environment appeared to be very plain and flat, making the environment have zero depth. Recommendation: remove the clock and add some form of art in the background versus a pegboard.
OK - recommendation to add props relevant to the product that's being shown. For example, a stack of printed-out papers, a pen cup, etc.
OK

FAIL - the wall, cabinet, and chair are very close, making this environment look fake and creating an unpassable walkway. Props are heavily weighted to one side, taking all of the focus away from the product itself. Recommendation: remove the clock and utilize some form of wall covering/art on the open white space behind the product, ensuring there's depth in the shot.

FAIL - the table is bending as the printer is shown flush alongside the wall, and the table is bending out from the wall. In addition, the placement of the clock would not appear in a "real life" scenario.
OK
OK
FAIL - too much white space in the background. In addition, the table appears to be non-rectangular, and is warping away from the wall.
